title: Define tiered resilience metrics and automated deployment gates for inference services
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Summary: This ticket captures a concrete, testable PRD for tiered SLA/SLOs and automated deployment gating for Redwood inference endpoints. Goal: provide deterministic acceptance criteria for model rollouts (hosted and dedicated) that balance latency, availability, and quality regressions while enabling automated canaries and rollbacks. The output will be a single canonical definition used by Console rollouts, CI pipelines, and runbooks.
scope: In scope: (1) Define SLO targets for three workload tiers (internal dev, standard customer, enterprise isolation) covering p50/p95/p99 latency for text generation and embeddings, 99.9/99.95 uptime windows, and request-level error budgets. (2) Define automated gating rules for canary percentage ramps, rollback thresholds (latency, error rate, quality drift), and mandatory human approval gates. (3) Acceptance tests and observability signals required to mark a rollout as Passed/Failed. (4) Hand-off checklist for Console UI and rollout automation engineers.
out_of_scope: Out of scope: per-model benchmarking methodology (handled by model-onboarding), pricing changes, deep infra rewrites. Platform-level QoS scheduling optimizations will be separate ENG epics.
proposed_slos: Tier: dev (internal): latency p50<=30ms p95<=120ms p99<=300ms; availability 99.5%; error budget 0.5% requests/day. Tier: standard (public customers): latency p50<=40ms p95<=180ms p99<=450ms; availability 99.9%; error budget 0.1% requests/day. Tier: enterprise-isolated (Dedicated/Private): latency p50<=25ms p95<=100ms p99<=250ms; availability 99.95%; error budget 0.05% requests/day. Notes: latency measured at token-level for generation requests with request types normalized (chat vs streaming). Availability measured as successful 2xx request rate across routing policy for the model variant.
error_budget_policy: Error budget accounting window = 7 days rolling. If consumed >50% in 7-day window -> throttle non-critical rollouts and open incident. If consumed >80% -> pause new model variants in that region and trigger mandatory postmortem. If consumed 100% -> trigger automated rollback to previous verified variant and route traffic to fallback model as defined by routing policy.
rollout_plan: Canary sequence: 1) Internal alpha: 0%->1% traffic for 3h synthetic + production shadowing. 2) Canary A: 1% for 24h (real traffic) with synthetic load spike tests at 2x baseline. 3) Canary B: 5% for 24h. 4) Ramp: 25% for 6h -> 50% for 3h -> 100% if all gates green. Automated rollback triggers: p95 latency regression >20% vs baseline OR error rate delta >0.05 absolute OR quality regression (evals) severity >=medium. If any gate fails, immediate rollback to previous variant and automatic paging to SRE.
quality_gates: Quality will be measured via: (a) Representative prompt eval set (PRD-defined) with acceptable metric thresholds (e.g., semantic-precision drop <2% absolute), (b) Production sampling-based metric: user-side rejection rate and unstructured QA signals aggregated. Quality gate enforcement: if eval regression exceeds threshold during any canary window, the deployment is paused and escalated to PM+ML owner for review.
monitoring_and_alerting: Required signals: latency histograms (token-level), request success rates, CPU/GPU utilization per model pool, KV cache hit ratio, LLM output quality metrics (from eval runner), and customer-facing error rates. Alerts: page on SLO breach or automated rollback event. Dashboards: per-model variant SLO panel, canary progress panel, error budget burn rate. Logging: linkable sample outputs (redacted) for QA.
acceptance_criteria: 1) CI synthetic test suite demonstrates p95 latency within target under 1.5x baseline traffic. 2) Canary run for 24h at 5% shows error budget consumption <=20% and no quality gate failures. 3) Console shows automated gate statuses and allows one-click rollback. 4) Runbook updated with paging thresholds and postmortem template. 5) E2E test that simulates a rollback path succeeds and previous variant restores traffic within 5 minutes.
risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Overly strict SLOs block benign changes -> mitigation: define temporary tolerances for experimental models and require PM approval for strict enforcement. Risk: False positives in quality evals -> mitigation: ensemble of eval metrics + manual spot checks for first two rollouts. Risk: Autoscale/infra flaps causing spurious gate failures -> mitigation: add infrastructure stability filter and require sustained signal for 10 minutes before automated rollback.
